title: {{NAME}} and the Cretaceous Crisis
moral: The most powerful forces in any situation are trust and clear thinking.
character_anchor: Bright children's book cartoon illustration, bold outlines, vivid flat colours. {{NAME}}, a young boy with brown hair and blue eyes, wearing a dark blue hero tunic with a gold dinosaur emblem, armoured dark trousers, and blue-gold boots — same child, same face, same exact outfit in every image.

pages.content:
The temporal fault opened above the palace at midnight.

Four Raptors, one Stegosaurus, and a very confused Pterosaur fell through it.

The palace was evacuated in two minutes, which was efficient.

The problem: Princess Helene had refused to evacuate and was in the courtyard trying to reason with the Stegosaurus.

The hero squad that arrived found her doing a reasonable job of it, actually.

{{NAME}}, the squad's youngest member, was the one who noticed: the princess wasn't just brave, she was effective.

pages.content:
The Raptors were the greater problem: they were coordinated, intelligent, and had cornered three heroes at the east wall.

But {{NAME}} had reviewed his dinosaur data: Raptors responded to authority signals. A specific posture, maintained steadily, read as dominance.

He walked toward them. Steadily. Directly. Maintaining the posture.

Princess Helene appeared at his shoulder.

Two humans, authority posture, unwavering.

The Raptors backed toward the wall and held there, watching.

"How did you know that?" said Princess Helene.

"Natural history library," said {{NAME}}.

pages.content:
The Pterosaur had gotten into the palace's map room and was methodically destroying the shelving.

Not aggressively: it seemed fascinated by the paper.

{{NAME}} entered the map room and, on a theory, presented it with the largest, most colourful map available.

The Pterosaur examined it for four minutes, made a satisfied sound, folded its wings, and sat on it.

Princess Helene arrived behind {{NAME}}.

"It wanted something to land on," she said.

"Something significant," he said. "Look: it chose the kingdom's original land survey."

pages.content:
The return portal was opened by the temporal team forty minutes later.

The Raptors went through calmly, as long as {{NAME}} and Princess Helene maintained their position until the last one was through.

The Stegosaurus walked through with the same dignity it had maintained throughout.

The Pterosaur had to be redirected from the map room with considerable negotiation, ultimately leaving the land survey behind, which the palace archivist declared an extraordinary act of theft.

"It can't come back to answer charges," said {{NAME}} gently.

pages.content:
After the debrief, Princess Helene and {{NAME}} sat in the palace kitchen waiting for the all-clear.

She said: "I was in the courtyard because I've read everything about prehistoric animals since I was five."

"That's exactly why I'm in this job," said {{NAME}}.

She looked at him. "The hero program has an opening for a prehistoric specialist."

"I know," he said. "I applied this morning. Before all this."

She almost laughed. "Good timing."

He went home and slept for eleven hours straight.
